record.title: GittinsEval reports near-zero model-selection regret at a fraction of exhaustive benchmark cost
record.summary: The arXiv v2 paper introduces GittinsEval, a Bayesian cost-aware policy for choosing which model configuration to evaluate next and when to stop. It combines Gittins-index allocation with an anytime recommendation rule for partially evaluated configurations. Replaying fixed response matrices from GSM8K, PIQA, AlpacaEval and MMLU, the authors report near-zero simple regret often using 1%–2% of exhaustive evaluation cost, with adaptive stopping commonly at 1%–10%. These are author-reported results on precomputed benchmark responses, not a live deployment study or independent reproduction. The claimed optimality is conditional on a Gaussian surrogate, independent configurations, conditionally i.i.d. item scores and predetermined costs; the paper explicitly does not provide a distribution-free finite-sample guarantee.
organizations: Shanghai University of Finance and Economics

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v2 preprint formulates LLM configuration selection as cost-aware Bayesian Markov-chain selection and proposes GittinsEval with index-based allocation, adaptive stopping and an anytime recommendation for partially evaluated configurations.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On fixed response matrices from GSM8K, PIQA, AlpacaEval and MMLU, the authors report near-zero simple regret often at 1%–2% of exhaustive-evaluation cost and adaptive stopping typically at 1%–10%. This is author-reported offline evaluation, not independent replication or a live deployment result.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The paper’s exact batch-level optimality proposition is conditional on a Gaussian surrogate, independent arms, conditionally i.i.d. scores and predetermined batch costs; the authors state it is not a distribution-free finite-sample identification guarantee for the realized response matrix.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: Reported cost is modeled using published API prices and per-configuration cost assumptions on precomputed response matrices; end-to-end savings in live evaluation pipelines, including operational overhead and changing prices, were not established.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the reported regret and evaluation-cost curves was performed.
Experiments replay precomputed response matrices and do not establish savings in live evaluations where configurations, prices, prompts or systems can change.

The formal guarantee depends on independent arms, a Gaussian model and predetermined costs; robustness under correlated configurations, nonstationary costs and misspecified score distributions is not established.

brief.importance_rationale: If its cost and recommendation-quality results transfer to operational model and prompt selection, adaptive evaluation could reduce a material recurring expense in model development and deployment. The score reflects that consequence if true; evidence is currently paper-reported replay on fixed benchmark response matrices under a specified statistical and cost model, without independent reproduction.
limitations: Results are author-reported on fixed response matrices from four benchmarks; no independent reproduction was performed.

The policy’s Bayesian optimality is conditional on the stated Gaussian surrogate, independent arms, conditional i.i.d. scores, and predetermined positive costs; numerical gridded indices and the anytime recommendation add further approximations.
The experiments do not establish performance in a live evaluation workflow or include complete operational costs beyond the modeled evaluation cost.
Simple regret and empirical benchmark recommendation do not establish statistical validity of benchmark claims, robustness to benchmark contamination, or broad model quality.

brief.summary: The arXiv v2 paper introduces GittinsEval, a Bayesian cost-aware policy for choosing which model configuration to evaluate next and when to stop. It combines Gittins-index allocation with an anytime recommendation rule for partially evaluated configurations. Replaying fixed response matrices from GSM8K, PIQA, AlpacaEval and MMLU, the authors report near-zero simple regret often using 1%–2% of exhaustive evaluation cost, with adaptive stopping commonly at 1%–10%. technical.claimed_result: Authors report near-zero simple regret using 1%–2% of exhaustive-evaluation cost in tested settings, with adaptive stopping commonly at 1%–10%.
technical.compute_or_cost: The reported 1%–2% and 1%–10% values are modeled evaluation cost relative to exhaustive evaluation on the tested response matrices. Live wall-clock, operational overhead and broader end-to-end savings are unmeasured.
technical.demonstrated_result: The preprint specifies a Bayesian cost-aware evaluation method and reports offline experiments. the research desk did not independently reproduce them.
technical.implementation_status: Research algorithm reported in an arXiv preprint; this review did not inspect or execute the linked code.
technical.mechanism: Treat each model configuration as an arm with a latent benchmark mean and configuration-dependent evaluation cost. A Gittins index combines expected score, uncertainty, cost and remaining horizon to allocate batches and stop; an uncertainty-penalized anytime rule can recommend a partly evaluated configuration.
technical.novelty: Adapts Gittins index allocation and stopping to a cost-aware benchmark recommendation objective and adds an anytime recommendation over partially observed configurations.
technical.regime: arXiv v2 replay on fixed response matrices for GSM8K, PIQA, AlpacaEval and MMLU, including large-candidate MMLU subject tasks. Costs are derived from published API prices. No live evaluation was performed in this review.
technical.reproducibility: Paper, protocol and appendices are available. Independent reproduction was not conducted.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares to configuration-level Bayesian optimization and cost-aware/cost-unaware bandit and racing baselines; advantages are strongest in large-example and large-candidate regimes.

brief.title: GittinsEval reports near-zero model-selection regret at a fraction of exhaustive benchmark cost
brief.why_it_matters: If it transfers beyond the tested response matrices, adaptive cost-aware evaluation could reduce the expense of comparing many model, prompt and decoding configurations, especially when inference costs differ. The reported savings do not establish general evaluation accuracy or live workflow savings; results rely on fixed response matrices and assumptions behind the policy.
